items.title: hnsw_ef accepts 0

probe_cases.desc: search with params.hnsw_ef=0 (semantically invalid; should be rejected)
probe_cases.observe: HTTP status and body. Bug: 200 OK returning result {id:1,score:1.0}. Fix: 400/422 with descriptive error.

items.expectation: Server should reject hnsw_ef<1 with 400/422 because an HNSW dynamic candidate list of size 0 cannot search. Other params like limit(min=1)/offset(min=0) are validated in OpenAPI; hnsw_ef should be too.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: hnsw_ef of 0 means 'consider zero candidates'; the OpenAPI/schema pattern validates limit>=1 and offset>=0, and SearchParams.hnsw_ef has no minimum.

items.title: [Bug]: Cosine similarity score strictly exceeds upper bound of 1.0 for identical vectors
setup: Use an external driver: for i in 0..100: generate a deterministic 128-dim float32 vector v, upsert {id:1,vector:v}, then search with the identical vector. Driver handles the loop; REST is called per iteration.

probe_cases.desc: search with the exact same vector that was just upserted, limit=1, with_payload
probe_cases.observe: Example search request shown with placeholder vector (driver substitutes it); observe returned score: Bug: score can exceed 1.0 (e.g. 1.0000001). Fixed: score clamps to >= -1.0 and <= 1.0; exact self-match yields 1.0.

items.expectation: For COSINE metric, the similarity score is mathematically bounded to [-1.0, 1.0]; an identical vector should score exactly 1.0 and never exceed it. Any value > 1.0 violates the metric contract.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: cosine similarity of a normalized vector to itself should be 1.0 (upper bound); f32 dot-product rounding can produce 1.0000001.

items.title: score_threshold_range_issue

probe_cases.desc: search with score_threshold=2.0 (above Cosine max)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 OK with empty result (threshold higher than any score). If Qdrant starts rejecting out-of-range thresholds, expect 400/422.

probe_cases.desc: search with score_threshold=-0.5 (below min score)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 OK returning the point (negative threshold passes everything). If rejection is added, expect 400/422.

items.expectation: score_threshold defines a minimum score filter. Values outside the Cosine score range [0,1] are semantically meaningless (2.0 returns empty, -0.5 returns all). Whether this is a defect is the subject of the issue; probe documents current behavior and tests whether new validation rejects it.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: semantic consistency of score as a threshold on similarity; no range constraint in OpenAPI/OpenAPI number type with no min/max.

items.title: Bug: Async upsert silently discards dimension-mismatched vectors (Poor Diagnostics)

probe_cases.desc: upsert 3-dim vector into 4-dim collection with wait omitted (async default)
probe_cases.observe: HTTP status/body, then GET /collections/test points_count. Bug: 200 {'status':'acknowledged'} and point discarded (count stays 0). Fix: reject with 4xx or surface a diagnostic.

probe_cases.desc: same operation with wait=true for comparison
probe_cases.observe: Control: should be 400 'Vector dimension error: expected dim: 4, got 3'. Confirms the validation exists only on the wait path.

items.expectation: Async (wait=false) upserts should not silently discard dimension-mismatched data while returning 200 success; at least the server should surface a diagnostic or reject, matching the wait=true behavior which returns 400.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: wait=true returns 400 with 'Vector dimension error', wait=false returns 200 'acknowledged' while discarding the point; acknowledged means received by WAL, not validated/stored.

items.title: Collection creation accepts `size=65536` despite FAQ stating maximum is 65,535 (off-by-one)

probe_cases.desc: create collection with size=65536 (FAQ says max 65535)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 accepted. If code aligned to FAQ, expect 422.

probe_cases.desc: create collection with size=65537 (above any stated max)
probe_cases.observe: Control: 422 rejected by both code and FAQ (upper bound is 65535/65536).

probe_cases.desc: create with size=65535 (FAQ max)
probe_cases.observe: Control: 200 accepted per FAQ.

items.expectation: Qdrant FAQ states dense vectors support up to 65,535 dimensions, so size=65536 should be rejected (or the FAQ updated). size=65536 currently accepted is the doc/code mismatch under test.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: FAQ says 'up to 65,535 dimensions'; code uses <=65536; maintainer @timvisee confirmed 'current limit for dense vectors is 65536'.

items.title: Bug: Empty vector `[]` upsert with `wait=false` can trigger server panic (zero-length assertion failure)

probe_cases.desc: upsert empty vector [] with wait=true (sync path)
probe_cases.observe: Control: 400 rejection (zero-length validation active on sync path).

probe_cases.desc: upsert empty vector [] with wait=false (async path)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 'acknowledged'. Risk: in sharded/distributed deployments a later search may hit a zero-length assertion (e.g. fixed_length_priority_queue 'length must be greater than zero') and panic the server. Also check server stays alive and count stays 0.

items.expectation: Zero-length vectors must be rejected at the API boundary (vector.is_empty()-style check or dim==0 validation), never reach code paths that assert non-zero length, and must not cause a server panic. Sync path already rejects; async path should not accept-and-risk-crash.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: try_from_flatten rejects dim==0 ('MultiDenseVector cannot have zero dimension'); validate_vector_parameters only in debug_assert; #7967 documents a 'length must be greater than zero' panic.

items.title: shard_number=0 and negative values accepted during collection creation

probe_cases.desc: create collection with shard_number=0
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 accepted (creates zero-shard collection). Fix: 400 'shard_number must be a positive integer'.

probe_cases.desc: create collection with shard_number=-1
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 accepted. Fix: 4xx rejecting non-positive shard_number.

items.expectation: shard_number must be a positive integer (>=1); 0 or negative values are invalid and should be rejected at the API boundary, consistent with replication_factor/write_consistency_factor which reject 0.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: shard_number=0 creates a collection with zero shards; other params in the same endpoint have validation (e.g. vectors.size upper bound).

items.title: Payload filter returns points with missing payload field (payload=None)
setup: Insert 10 points (wait=true): even ids color=red, odd ids color=blue, ids 3 and 6 have NO color payload at all (see issue body exact payloads).

probe_cases.desc: search with must filter color=red, limit=10, with_payload=true
probe_cases.observe: Bug: response includes points with payload=None or missing color (ids 3,6). Correct: only 4 even-red points (ids 1,4,7,9) returned, missing-key points excluded.

items.expectation: A must+match condition on a payload key must only return points whose key exists and equals the value. Points missing the key must be excluded since a missing key cannot satisfy a match. (GT labels this FP_NOT_REPRO, so running it tests whether the reported corruption actually reproduces.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: a match condition requires the key to exist and value to match; a missing key cannot satisfy a match and should return false.

items.title: Bug: Batch operations partially apply despite returning HTTP 400 error (atomicity violation)

probe_cases.desc: POST a mixed batch: 2 valid 4-dim + 1 invalid 3-dim point
probe_cases.observe: If atomic: return 400 or 422 AND count stays 3. If non-atomic: returns 400 but count increased (bug). Note: issue body reports this as state-dependent; may not reproduce on a fresh container.

items.expectation: A batch returning an error (4xx) should apply no operations; point count should remain unchanged. A 4xx response means the request was rejected and no state modified. (GT is SELF_CLOSED; probe tests whether partial-apply reproduces or is correct.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: batch returns 400 'Vector dimension error' but count 3->5 (valid points persisted); standard REST contract says 4xx means no state modified.

items.title: Bug: Payload index returns incorrect filtered results — index corruption after creation

probe_cases.desc: scroll/filter for category_id=cat_a, limit=100
probe_cases.observe: Bug: returns far fewer than 25 (issue observed 2 points). Correct: all 25 cat_a points. Count GET /collections/test_index should still show 50 (data intact, index query wrong).

items.expectation: After a keyword payload index is built with wait=true (HTTP 200), an indexed-field filter for cat_a should return all 25 matching points. A significant miss rate (2/25) with correct point count is an index/query correctness defect. (GT is SELF_CLOSED; probe tests reproduction.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: after creating a keyword index on category_id with wait=true, filtered search returns only 2 of 25 matching points.

items.title: Bug: Named vector lifecycle operations (update+delete) corrupt search — returns 400
setup: Insert 20 points with named vector image_vector values (wait=true).
Put named-vector index on image_vector if applicable.

probe_cases.desc: search via named vector image_vector (baseline)
probe_cases.observe: Baseline: 200 OK with results.

probe_cases.desc: update named vectors on some points
probe_cases.observe: Expect 200.

probe_cases.desc: delete named vectors from points ids 1 and 2
probe_cases.observe: Expect 200; then count GET /collections/test_named still 20.

probe_cases.desc: search again via named vector after update+delete lifecycle
probe_cases.observe: Bug (per issue): returns 400 'broken'. Correct: 200 with results for remaining points.

items.expectation: Search via a named vector must keep working after vector update+delete lifecycle operations on specific points; the collection remains intact (count unchanged) and searches should return results. (GT is SELF_CLOSED; probe tests reproduction.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: after insert->update->delete of named vectors, subsequent named-vector search returns HTTP 400 while point count stays 20.

items.title: Bug: Batch operations not atomic — valid points persisted despite HTTP 400 error
setup: Run significant preceding CRUD on the container, because issue reports it is state-dependent (may not reproduce on a fresh container).
Upsert 3 valid 4-dim points (ids 1,2,3); record baseline count=3.

probe_cases.desc: mixed batch 2 valid + 1 invalid (dim=3)
probe_cases.observe: Issue: HTTP 400 returned but GET /collections/test_batch2/points/count shows count 3->5 (valid points persisted). Correct (atomic): 400 and count unchanged at 3. Note BY_DESIGN: Qdrant may reject-with-partial-apply by design; probe documents which behavior the current version exhibits.

items.expectation: Whether a 400 on a batch must roll back all operations. Standard REST 'rejected' semantics imply no state change, but Qdrant may define batch as non-transactional. Probe records the actual behavior on the target version. (GT is BY_DESIGN.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: batch handler validates per-operation; writes may already be dispatched when a later operation fails, so valid points persist despite the 400.

items.title: Strict mode inconsistently validates zero values — allows creation of unusable collections

probe_cases.desc: control: strict_mode_config.max_query_limit=0 (correctly rejected)
probe_cases.observe: Correct: 422 'max_query_limit: value 0 invalid, must be 1 or larger'.

probe_cases.desc: filter_max_conditions=0 (the defect)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 accepted, creating a poisoned collection. Then any scroll with a filter condition fails 400 'Filter condition limit reached (1 > 0)'.

probe_cases.desc: upsert_max_batchsize=0 (the defect)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 accepted; subsequent upsert fails 400 'Limit exceeded 1 > 0 for upsert limit'.

items.expectation: All limit-type fields in strict_mode_config should have consistent validation. max_query_limit/max_timeout/max_points_count reject 0; filter_max_conditions and upsert_max_batchsize should also reject values < 1 instead of creating an unusable collection.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: consistency matrix shows 3 fields reject 0 (422) while filter_max_conditions and upsert_max_batchsize accept 0 (200) producing a poisoned collection.

items.title: Bug: Payload index silently returns severely incomplete results — 2/25 matching points after wait:true
setup: Issue reports state-dependence: a fresh container returns correct results. To reproduce, run sustained CRUD for hours (create/delete 10+ collections, thousands of points, index build/drop) first.

probe_cases.desc: filter for category_id=cat_a after index build
probe_cases.observe: Bug: returns 2 of 25 (92% miss). Correct: all 25. GET /collections/test_idx2 count should be 50 (data intact). Control run on a fresh container returns 25/25.

items.expectation: With wait=true (index build returns 200), once the index is built all existing points must be queryable via the indexed field; cat_a filter should return 25. A persistent 2/25 result with intact point count is an index-completeness defect. (GT is FP_NOT_REPRO; probe tests reproduction.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: wait param means 'wait for changes to actually happen before responding'; index returned 200 but indexed field filter returned only 2/25.

items.title: `vectors={}` silently accepted during collection creation — produces unusable collection

probe_cases.desc: create collection with vectors={} (empty object)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 accepted. (Also verify collection exists via GET /collections/broken.) Then PUT /collections/broken/points returns 400 'Default vector config is not found in collection'. Whether that creation acceptance is a defect is the subject (GT=FP_BY_DESIGN).

probe_cases.desc: confirm the poisoned collection is unusable
probe_cases.observe: Retrospectively demonstrates collection has no default vector config; insert fails 400.

items.expectation: A collection should either be created with usable vector config or rejected; accepting vectors={} creates an unusable collection whose insert fails. (GT is FP_BY_DESIGN: Qdrant may allow vectorless collections by design; probe records actual behavior.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: API doc marks vectors required=false; vectors={} accepted 200 then any point op fails 'Default vector config is not found in collection'.

items.title: Missing `vectors` field silently accepted during collection creation — produces unusable collection

probe_cases.desc: create collection without a vectors field
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 accepted (collection exists, no vector config). Then any point op fails 400 'Default vector config is not found'. (GT=FP_BY_DESIGN.)

items.expectation: Whether omitting vectors must be rejected. If Qdrant intentionally supports vectorless collections, omitting is legitimate; otherwise it should be 422. Probe records actual behavior (creation acceptance + subsequent insert failure). (GT is FP_BY_DESIGN.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: vectors is object required=false; omitting it still returns 200 but the collection cannot serve vector ops.

items.title: `filter.should=null` silently accepted in query/search — null filter condition ignored

probe_cases.desc: query with filter.should=null
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 OK returning both points (null filter silently ignored, no filtering). If strict: 4xx rejecting null for an array-typed field. Control for contrast: filter.should='some_string' returns 400 type error but null returns 200.

items.expectation: filter.should is documented as an array of conditions; explicit null is not a valid value and should be rejected rather than silently ignored as 'no filter'. A null should not be indistinguishable from an absent field. (GT is FP_BY_DESIGN; probe records actual behavior.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: string value is rejected but null is accepted-and-ignored; serde maps JSON null to Option::None, indistinguishable from absent.

items.title: `filter.must_not` accepts object instead of array — type mismatch silently ignored

probe_cases.desc: query with filter.must_not as a single object instead of array
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 returning all points (object silently ignored, must_not not applied). If strict: 400 type mismatch 'expected a sequence'. Note expected correct filter would exclude tag=x leaving only tag=y.

items.expectation: filter.must_not is an array of conditions; a single object is a type mismatch that should be rejected (as other type mismatches are), not silently ignored, so that exclusion filters are not silently dropped. (GT is FP_BY_DESIGN; probe records actual behavior.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: must_not expects an array; passing an object returns 200 with unfiltered results, type mismatch not surfaced.

items.title: `query=null` silently accepted — returns all points instead of being rejected

probe_cases.desc: query with query=null
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 returning all points ordered by ID [1,5,10] (null query silently falls back to 'no query'). If strict: 4xx rejecting null. The doc fallback (return-by-ID) is specified for an ABSENT query, not explicit null.

items.expectation: An explicit query=null is semantically invalid and should be rejected, not treated as 'no query' returning all points by ID. The documented return-by-ID fallback applies only when query is absent. (GT is FP_BY_DESIGN; probe records actual behavior.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: docs say 'if missing without prefetches, returns points ordered by ID' — describes absent query, not explicit null.

items.title: `POST /cluster/recover` returns HTTP 500 in standalone mode — should return 4xx

probe_cases.desc: call cluster recover in standalone mode
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 500 'Service internal error: Qdrant is running in standalone mode'. Fix: 4xx (400/405) 'Cluster operations not available'. The error body already correctly names standalone mode; it is the status class that is wrong.

items.expectation: Calling a cluster-only operation on a standalone instance is a client error, not a server failure; the HTTP status should be 4xx (400 Bad Request or 405), never 500 internal-server-error.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: RFC 7231 — 4xx is client error, 5xx is server failure; predictable standalone mode should be 4xx, body correctly names the cause.

items.title: Server crash on collection creation with shard_number=INT_MAX — missing upper-bound validation unlike replication_factor

probe_cases.desc: create collection with shard_number=2147483647 (INT_MAX)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: request hangs ~25s then connection closed (curl 52 'Empty reply'); server becomes unresponsive. Fix: 400/422 validation. Monitor server health after (GET / should respond).

probe_cases.desc: control: replication_factor=0 correctly rejected
probe_cases.observe: Compare: 422 'replication_factor: value 0 invalid...' — demonstrates validation exists for replication_factor but missing for shard_number upper bound.

items.expectation: The server should validate shard_number and reject an extreme value (e.g. INT_MAX) with 400/422 rather than attempting to allocate billions of shards and crashing/hanging. A syntactically valid parameter must never take down the server.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: shard_number=2147483647 causes resource allocation for 2B+ shards -> hang + connection close; replication_factor=0 is properly rejected with 422 showing inconsistent validation.

items.title: Silent data loss: named vector upsert in single-vector collection returns 200 OK but point is discarded

probe_cases.desc: upsert a point using named vector format into a single-vector collection
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 {'status':'acknowledged'} but point NOT stored. Verify with POST /collections/test_named_vec/points/count {"exact":true} -> count 0 (silent data loss).

probe_cases.desc: control: wrong-dimension vector correctly rejected
probe_cases.observe: Compare: 400 'Vector dimension error: expected dim: 4, got 6' — shows dimension is validated but format is not.

items.expectation: The vector format (named vs unnamed) must match the collection configuration; upserting a named vector into a single-vector (unnamed) collection should be rejected with 4xx, not silently accepted with 200 while discarding the point. Silent data loss with a success response violates the write contract.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: collection has unnamed vectors; named-vector format is accepted 200/acknowledged but point discarded (count=0); wrong-dimension is correctly rejected 400.

items.title: Query API silently returns 200 OK when lookup_from references a non-existent collection
setup: Seed source with 5 points (ids 0..4, payload tag/category) wait=true.

probe_cases.desc: query source with lookup_from.collection pointing at a NON-EXISTENT collection
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 returning source results as if lookup_from ignored. Correct: 404/400 'Collection not found' for the lookup target.

probe_cases.desc: control: same query with a VALID lookup_from.collection
probe_cases.observe: Control: 200 OK (lookup target exists). Confirms the only difference is existence of the referenced collection.

items.expectation: lookup_from.collection references a cross-collection lookup source that must exist; a non-existent collection should produce 404 (or 400), not a silent 200 that makes the lookup indistinguishable from being ignored. (Per API reference lookup collection must exist.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: API reference requires the lookup collection to exist; v1.18.2 does not validate its existence and returns 200 with source results.

items.title: Search offset pagination returns duplicate point IDs across pages (HNSW approximation)
setup: Seed 25 points (ids 0..24) with the sequential vectors and payload in the issue body, wait=true.

probe_cases.desc: page 1: search offset=0 limit=10
probe_cases.observe: Record returned point IDs.

probe_cases.desc: page 2: search offset=10 limit=10
probe_cases.observe: Record IDs; check overlap with page 1. Issue observed duplicates (e.g. ids 11,22,23,24).

probe_cases.desc: page 3: search offset=20 limit=10
probe_cases.observe: Record IDs; check additional overlap. Issue: union has 25 total with only 19 unique.

probe_cases.desc: control via scroll (cursor pagination, non-overlapping)
probe_cases.observe: Control: scroll returns non-overlapping results — contrast with offset search.

items.expectation: Standard pagination implies successive pages are non-overlapping and union to the full result set. If HNSW approximation cannot guarantee this, offset pagination may return duplicates; the issue discusses documenting or auto-exact. (GT is BY_DESIGN; probe records whether duplicates still occur.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: offset pagination with HNSW is non-deterministic; scroll cursor pagination does not have this problem.

items.title: Invalid filter conditions silently accepted (200 OK) with poor error diagnostics across search/query/scroll endpoints

probe_cases.desc: search with an empty must array
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 returning results (empty must accepted). If validation added: 400. Issue expects empty arrays rejected.

probe_cases.desc: search referencing a non-existent payload field
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 with empty results (field not validated). If validation added: reject.

probe_cases.desc: search with a contradictory range (gt>lt)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: 200 with empty results. If validation added: 400 'gt must be < lt'.

probe_cases.desc: diagnostics: filter with a null key (rejected but message quality)
probe_cases.observe: Already rejected (400) but observe the error text: poor = raw serde 'Invalid type unit value ... at line 1 column N' without naming the 'key' parameter.

items.expectation: Invalid or self-contradictory filter conditions should be rejected with clear, parameter-naming error messages rather than silently returning 200. Cases under test: empty arrays, non-existent fields, contradictory ranges, and diagnostic quality for actually-rejected conditions.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: 5 classes of invalid filters silently accepted (empty must, nonexistent field, type mismatch, contradictory range, wrong structure); rejected cases lack parameter names in serde messages.

items.title: Systemic: serde deserialization errors across 7 endpoints expose Rust internal types (usize/u32/f32) and lack parameter names

probe_cases.desc: search limit=-1 (type underflow for usize)
probe_cases.observe: Poor: 400 'invalid value: integer -1, expected usize at line 1 column N' (leaks Rust type, no param name). Quality improved if message is 'limit must be a positive integer'.

probe_cases.desc: search score_threshold as a string
probe_cases.observe: Poor: 400 '... expected f32 at line 1 column N'.

probe_cases.desc: recommend strategy as integer
probe_cases.observe: Poor: 400 'invalid type: integer 123, expected string or map'. Contrast strategy='invalid' -> 400 listing enum values (good diagnostic).

probe_cases.desc: scroll limit=-1
probe_cases.observe: Poor: 400 '... expected usize'. Same pattern.

probe_cases.desc: query limit=-1
probe_cases.observe: Poor: 400 '... expected usize'.

items.expectation: Error messages for invalid parameter values should name the parameter, use domain-friendly type names (positive integer instead of usize), and not require JSON column counting. These are diagnostics-quality (contract/enum) expectations, not functional correctness.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: serde echoes Rust types (usize/u32/f32) and column offsets without parameter names; application-level validation (e.g. limit=0 -> 422 names param) proves Qdrant can produce good messages.

items.title: Write operations accept `timeout=0` despite the OpenAPI schema declaring `minimum: 1`

probe_cases.desc: set payload with timeout=0 (forbidden by schema minimum:1)
probe_cases.observe: Bug (doc/code mismatch): 200 with status completed/ok. If server enforced schema, expect 422. Also report whether timeout=0 is treated as valid (no-wait) by comparing to timeout=1 which also returns 200.

probe_cases.desc: same call with timeout=1 (documented minimum) for comparison
probe_cases.observe: Control: 200 OK. If timeout=0 and timeout=1 behave identically, the schema minimum:1 is not enforced.

items.expectation: The OpenAPI schema declares timeout (integer minimum:1) on write operations. Either the server must reject timeout=0 with 422, or timeout=0 carries valid 'no-wait' semantics and the schema should be minimum:0. The runtime behavior and published contract must agree.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: OpenAPI declares timeout as integer minimum:1; server accepts 0 with 200 on set payload/delete/create/update vectors — schema/code discrepancy.

items.title: OpenAPI schema for `VectorParams.size` is missing the enforced `maximum: 65536` constraint

probe_cases.desc: fetch the published OpenAPI schema to inspect VectorParams.size
probe_cases.observe: In components.schemas.VectorParams.properties.size: bug = {'minimum':1} with NO maximum. Sibling DenseVectorConfig.properties.size has {'minimum':1,'maximum':65536}. Missing maximum = schema/implementation mismatch.

probe_cases.desc: runtime: create collection with size=70000 (>65536)
probe_cases.observe: Runtime enforces 422 'vectors.size: value 70000 invalid, must be from 1 to 65536' even though schema has no maximum; run with a NEW collection name distinct from c1.

items.expectation: The OpenAPI schema should declare maximum:65536 on VectorParams.size to match the server's enforced 65536 upper bound, so schema-driven clients see the same limit (contract = implementation). If size>65536 is intended valid, the server bound should change; the schema and runtime must agree.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: server rejects size=70000 with 422 'must be from 1 to 65536' but VectorParams.size schema only declares minimum:1; DenseVectorConfig.size already has maximum:65536.

items.title: `count` `exact=false` on `is_empty` under-counts ~35% consistently; `is_null` on the same field is correct
setup: Data structure: total N=200 (also try 500, 1000); for i in 0..N-1, point id=i+1, vector=[1,0]; if i%5 != 0 give payload {"kw":"red"} else NO kw field (so is_empty matches the ~20% missing-kw points). wait=true.
PUT /collections/c/index {"field_name":"kw","field_schema":"keyword"}  (integer field schema is keyword here)
Sleep ~3s after indexing so the count runs at steady state (outside the documented 'unreliable during indexing' window).

probe_cases.desc: count exact=true on is_empty kw (ground truth)
probe_cases.observe: Returns correct count (e.g. ~40 of 200).

probe_cases.desc: count exact=false on is_empty kw (the defect)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: under-counts ~-35% consistently (e.g. 25 vs 40).

probe_cases.desc: control: is_null on the same field
probe_cases.observe: Control: returns correct (0) on both paths — isolates the bug to is_empty estimation, not the field/index.

items.expectation: At steady state (after indexing), count exact=false should approximate exact=true. The documentation only warns approximate counts 'might be unreliable during the indexing process'; a consistent ~35% is_empty under-count at steady state falls outside that caveat. (Per OpenAPI: exact=false means approximate count faster.)
items.contract_hint: Issue body: OpenAPI declares exact=false 'approximate count might be unreliable during indexing'; is_empty under-counts ~35% at steady state while is_null is exact-correct, isolating the estimator path.

items.title: `count` `exact=false` on numeric/datetime `range` filter returns bidirectionally-wrong counts (histogram estimator)
setup: Data: N=500 (also 200/1000/10000), seeded with random.Random(42); point id=i+1, vector=[1,0], payload {"n": random.randint(0,1000)}. wait=true.

probe_cases.desc: count exact=true on range n 100..200 (ground truth)
probe_cases.observe: Correct count (e.g. ~50).

probe_cases.desc: count exact=false on the same range (the defect)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: off by +/-5-10% (e.g. 46 vs 50).

probe_cases.desc: count exact=false on range gte:500
probe_cases.observe: Observe error direction flips (+7% per issue): some ranges over-count, others under-count.

probe_cases.desc: count exact=false on range lte:300
probe_cases.observe: Observe error (-8% per issue); bidirectional error confirms histogram estimator bias, not a fixed fallback.

items.expectation: At steady state count exact=false should track exact=true; the docs only disclaim reliability 'during the indexing process'. A bidirectional +/-5-10% steady-state error on range counts (with exact=true always correct) violates that contract.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: FieldCondition.range 'check if points value lies in a given range'; exact=false uses a histogram estimator with stable +/-5-10% error at steady state; exact=true always correct.

items.title: `count` `exact=false` on compound filter under-counts 20-60% when conditions touch the same field (independence assumption)
setup: Data: N=500 (also 200/1000/10000), random.Random(42); kws=[red,blue,green,yellow]; point id=i+1, vector=[1,0], payload {"kw":random.choice(kws),"cat":random.choice(["x","y"])}. wait=true.
Index both fields: PUT /collections/c/index for kw (keyword) and cat (keyword).

probe_cases.desc: control: single condition must kw=red, exact=true and false
probe_cases.observe: Control: single-condition exact=false should equal exact=true (~130) — the leaf estimator is correct.

probe_cases.desc: same-field compound: must kw=red AND must_not kw=blue
probe_cases.observe: Bug: under-counts (issue ~130 vs ~100, -23%). Correct: red excludes blue => result set is exactly red, so count should equal the single-condition count (~130).

probe_cases.desc: cross-field compound: must kw=red AND must cat=x
probe_cases.observe: Also under-counts (issue ~73 vs ~62, -14%) — independence assumption is wrong for same-field and milder for cross-field.

items.expectation: At steady state, count exact=false on a compound filter should approximate the true count; the estimator assumes condition independence (P(A AND B) ≈ P(A)*P(B)), which under-counts same-field mutually-exclusive conditions (red AND NOT blue == red). The docs only disclaim reliability 'during the indexing process'.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: cardinality estimator assumes independence across combined conditions; same-field (red AND must_not blue) under-counts ~20-60% while single-condition is exact.

items.title: `count` `exact=false` on `geo_radius` degenerates: medium radii collapse to a fixed value, large radii return the collection total
setup: Data: N=1000; random.Random(42); point id=i+1, vector=[1,0], payload {"loc":{"lat":random.uniform(-89,89),"lon":random.uniform(-179,179)}}. wait=true.

probe_cases.desc: count exact=true on geo_radius 2000km (center 0,0)
probe_cases.observe: Correct exact count (issue: ~18).

probe_cases.desc: count exact=false on geo_radius 2000km (the defect)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: collapses to fixed ~133 regardless of true count (issue +639%).

probe_cases.desc: count exact=false on geo_radius 5000km vs 2000km
probe_cases.observe: Bug: also returns ~133 even though true count is much larger (~112) — two very different radii give the same fixed estimate.

probe_cases.desc: count exact=false on a large geo_radius 10000km
probe_cases.observe: Bug: returns collection total (1000) for true 503 — saturates to total.

items.expectation: At steady state, count exact=false on a geo_radius filter should track the radius's true selectivity; collapsing to a fixed sub-fraction or saturating to the collection total violates the approximate-count contract. Docs only disclaim reliability 'during the indexing process'; exact=true is always correct.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: FieldCondition.geo_radius 'check if geo point is within a given radius'; estimator degenerates at medium radii (fixed value) and large radii (returns total), worst +639% error.

items.title: `count` `exact=false` on `match_any` (multi-value) under-counts, increasingly with value count (independent-OR assumption)
setup: Data: N=500; random.Random(42); kws=[red,blue,green,yellow,purple]; point id=i+1, vector=[1,0], payload {"kw":random.choice(kws)}. wait=true.

probe_cases.desc: control: match_any single value [red], exact=false
probe_cases.observe: Control: single value is exact-correct on both paths (issue: 107=107).

probe_cases.desc: match_any two values [red,blue], exact=false (the defect)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: under-counts (issue -11%, 189 vs 213).

probe_cases.desc: match_any five values, exact=false (all kws, whole field)
probe_cases.observe: Bug: under-count grows (-33%, 337 vs 500) even though match_any of all five covers the entire field and should equal total.

items.expectation: At steady state, count exact=false on match_any should approximate exact=true. For single keyword fields the values are mutually exclusive so the true count is the sum of per-value counts (capped at total); the independent-OR estimator under-counts and the error grows with the number of values. Docs only disclaim 'during indexing'.
items.contract_hint: Issue body: MatchAny 'exact match on any of the given values'; estimator uses independent-OR 1-prod(1-p_i) which is always below the mutually-exclusive sum and grows with value count.
